instruction: Use Abaqus via the Command Line Interface (CLI) or Python scripting environment to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric finite-element model of a circular plate. Adopt the N-mm-MPa unit system throughout. Geometry: Create a 2D axisymmetric deformable solid part representing the circular plate cross-section. The radial extent is from r = 0 mm to r = 50 mm. The axial/thickness extent is from z = 0 mm to z = 1 mm. Material: Define a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3. Assign this material to the entire plate section using a homogeneous solid section. Mesh and Element Type: Employ CAX4R axisymmetric solid elements. Use a structured mesh with a radial seed size of 2.0 mm and one element through the thickness. Create the following node sets: AXIS on the r = 0 boundary, OUTER on the r = 50 mm boundary, and TOP on the z = 1 mm boundary. Boundary Conditions: On AXIS, constrain radial displacement U1 = 0. On OUTER, constrain both U1 = 0 and U2 = 0. Loading: Apply a downward pressure of 0.1 N/mm² on the TOP boundary, represented as equivalent axisymmetric concentrated nodal forces. For each top node at radius r_i, compute the force in the U2 direction as: F_i = -p × 2πr_i × Δr_i For the first and last top nodes, use half the adjacent radial interval for Δr_i. For interior top nodes, use half the distance between neighboring top nodes. The node at r = 0 carries zero equivalent force. Analysis: Create a static analysis step named Step-Pressure. Request field output for U, RF, and S. Create and submit a job named Job-Plate, and wait for successful completion. Deliverables: Save the model database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Plate.cae and the output database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Plate.odb. [Software] To start Abaqus/CAE, run `C:\SIMULIA\EstProducts\2023\win_b64\resources\install\cmdDirFeature\launcher.bat cae` (adjust path to your install).
